narrative:
The model predicts you have a 92% chance of leaving your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization. These stood out as the top drivers compared with everything else in your profile.

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees who stay have shorter experience (half have only 1–5 years), your mid-level tenure matches people who tend to move on once they have built a solid background. Similarly, having received other job opportunities strongly increased the likelihood of leaving; most employees predicted to stay (77%) had not received any outside offers, so this factor worked against you. Finally, your 1–5 years in your current role also nudged the prediction upward. This is actually the most common length of time for employees who stay, but combined with your other experience and external offers, the model interpreted it as a sign you may be ready for a change.

The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to explore whether additional responsibilities, better recognition of your experience, or clearer paths to advancement could change your outlook and reduce the risk of leaving.
